incident-bot: ALERT: Canary p99 latency breach detected for model-redwood-v12 in region-us-west-2. p95=420ms (SLO 200ms), p99=3.6s (SLO 500ms), error rate 0.4%. Autoscale status: nominal.

Dana-oncall: seeing it too — major spike starting ~5189994200. Streaming stalls reported (clients time out at ~2.5s). Paging Frank.

Frank-sre: on it. grabbing graphs. can you paste the canary config?

Alice-ml: canary was rolled ~10m ago to v12-quant-opt. Traffic shift 5% -> 20% over 8m with gradual ramp. No config changes besides quantization.

Ben-platform: adding live traces: https://perf.redwood/trace/5189994321 (posted) — tail calls show long KV lookup times and several mux queue backlogs.

Frank-sre: pulling logs from serving runtime. suspicious lines:
```
2026-07-21T09:12:03Z [worker-7] kv-cache: miss 1.3s (warmup)
2026-07-21T09:12:04Z [mux] enqueue_delay=240ms
2026-07-21T09:12:05Z [runtime] encode_step: 1.7s
```

Dana-oncall: hmm kv warmup miss of 1.3s is bad. Could be cache eviction leading to repeated cold lookups under shifted traffic. Any recent eviction/resize?

Ben-platform: autoscaler didn't change pool size. Cache eviction logs show a concurrent GC at 09:11:58. I think warmup overlap with increased traffic.

Alice-ml: v12 uses a larger kv footprint (attention key size increase after optimizer change). That could explain more frequent evictions on small hosts.

Gina-pm: customer impact — CS reported a handful of 504s from power-user accounts hitting chat streaming last 15m. Evan, can you confirm and triage customer impact?

Evan-support: confirmed ~8 customer incidents escalated to support, mostly streaming timeouts. Not billing-critical but noticeable UX degradation for chat. Notifying top-tier customers now.

Frank-sre: immediate mitigations proposed:
- throttle canary traffic back to 5% (stop ramp)
- enable model fallback to v11 for streaming paths (route streaming requests to stable variant)
- bump cache size on canary nodes (temporary)
- consider rapid rollback if no improvement in 5-10m

Dana-oncall: executing throttle now: `redwood ctl deploy adjust-split --service=canary-model --percent=5`

Ben-platform: split adjusted. Traffic ramp halted and rollback gating enabled.

Frank-sre: enabling fallback routing for streaming via routing policy: `routes.add --from=model-redwood-v12 --to=model-redwood-v11 --match=streaming` (doing dry-run then apply)

Alice-ml: enabling fallback. note: v11 has slightly different tokenization but acceptable for streaming stability.

Ben-platform: increased cache alloc on canary hosts: `infractl mempool resize --pool=kv-cache --size=1.5x --nodes=canary` — applying.

Frank-sre: after throttle + fallback + cache bump: p95 now 210ms, p99 560ms, streaming errors dropped from 0.9%->0.2%. Improvements visible at 5189995200.

Dana-oncall: good. but p99 still slightly above SLO (560ms). Is that due to remaining cold misses?

Frank-sre: digging deeper — a small set (~7%) of requests still hitting cold paths because of keyspace skew: hot prefixes aren't properly cached due to different prefix hashing in v12. Patch incoming to normalize hashing on fallback path.

Alice-ml: trying a model-side quick patch to reduce kv footprint for streaming: `quantize_kv=true` (toggle) — will push as feature flag to canary only.

Frank-sre: agree low-risk to flip feature flag. Applying now.

ci-bot: DEPLOY NOTE: feature-flag `quantize_kv=true` rolled to model-redwood-v12-canary at 09:21:30Z. CI checks passed.

Ben-platform: after flag flip p99 = 460ms, p95 = 180ms, streaming error rate <0.1% at 5189995400. Looks stable for last 2m.

Gina-pm: customer comms: drafted message for affected customers explaining temporary degraded experience during canary rollout and that fixes applied; offering a short incident summary. Evan please review.

Evan-support: reviewed, sending notifications now. will include mitigation steps and ETA for stable rollout resumption.

Dana-oncall: decision time: keep canary pinned at 5% with fallback enabled and monitor 30m; do NOT continue ramp. If p99 <500ms for 15m, consider gradual ramp with KV patch baked in. Otherwise rollback to v11.

Frank-sre: agree. I'll keep monitoring tail latencies and KV hit rates. will handoff in 30m to next oncall if stable.

Dana-oncall: adding handoff note for next shift:
- cause suspected: increased KV footprint in v12 + cache eviction + hashing mismatch
- mitigations applied: throttled canary to 5%, enabled streaming fallback to v11, increased cache pool, toggled `quantize_kv` flag
- current state: p95=180-220ms, p99=420-480ms, error-rate <0.1%
- actions for followup: monitor kv_hit_ratio, mux enqueue_delay, and ramp only after 15m stable p99<500ms

Frank-sre: tagging dashboards: KV hit ratio: https://dash.redwood/kv/5189994321, tail traces: https://perf.redwood/trace/5189994321/detail

Evan-support: CS notified customers at 09:25Z, some asked for postmortem. Gina — can we schedule a short postmortem with owners (platform, ml, sres) to outline long-term fixes?

Gina-pm: yes scheduling now. triage doc: https://docs.redwood/incident/5189994321 (draft)

Dana-oncall: handing off to Frank in 30m if stable. Leaving incident channel open. :white_check_mark:

Frank-sre: acknowledged. I'll keep an eye and escalate to rollback if p99 rebounds.

ci-bot: INCIDENT: status=mitigated, summary="Canary v12 induced KV warmup -> p99 spike. mitigations applied: throttle, fallback, cache bump, quantize_kv flag"
